summary: The verified 32-bit input ceiling limits every legal Excel title to at most seven characters, which is too small for an honest runtime-scaling verdict by output length.

workload_bound.source_constraint: The source-fidelity-verified bound 1 <= columnNumber <= 2^31 - 1 implies a bijective base-26 title of at most seven characters.

replacement_checks.evidence: Each loop iteration subtracts one, performs one division by 26, and appends exactly one output character. The quotient strictly decreases, so there are exactly k iterations and O(k) = O(log n) time with only the output buffer growing.
Black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition, including the app-local conversion and returned-string path.
